candidates.title: 校園聲音探索展
candidates.prompt:
Redraw the reference images into a NEW illustrated website opening scene for Taiwan middle-school Unit 3.3, CHARACTERISTICS OF SOUND. Use reference characters and warm richly painted anime storybook rendering, honey-colored wood, inviting sunlight. Xiaokui: brown eyes, BROWN DOUBLE BUN HAIR with loose wisps and bangs, ivory hoodie and dark/brown backpack straps; no single ponytail or green straps. Grandpa: fluffy silver-white hair, round thin glasses, ABSOLUTELY CLEAN SHAVEN, white coat over brown waistcoat and tie. Both full heads and natural hands clearly visible, essential elements within central 90% of frame. Wide landscape 16:9, one unified believable story scene, NOT collage, NOT an infographic or seven-panel poster.
LATEST USER PRIORITY: EACH candidate must represent MANY of the seven learning sections together, not just two instruments and not just one narrow activity. Stage an inviting SCHOOL SOUND EXPLORATION EVENT, with foreground conversation/listening and several legible sound props, middle-ground hearing clues, background school performance/movie setting. A deliberate hierarchy, generous space between grouped objects: rich but organized, joyful inquiry rather than clutter.
EACH IMAGE MUST INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING SIX IDENTIFIABLE GROUPS, not omit whole groups:
A. Compact wooden SINGLE-STRING sound box on a table, one taut metallic string, two bridges including a small movable bridge, one tuning peg, visible plucking gesture or ready position. This connects amplitude/loudness and string length/tension/pitch.
B. THREE simple STRAIGHT HOLLOW OPEN-ENDED pipes of visibly different lengths, same bore/material, arranged horizontally on an open support with cut circular mouths visible. NOT closed-bottom panpipes, not bent plumbing, not water-filled glass bottles. This connects air-column length and pitch.
C. A clearly recognizable pair of silver U-SHAPED TUNING FORKS of unequal lengths, each with TWO parallel prongs joined by a rounded U and a stem, beside a small rubber-headed striker, on a small wood block. These supply a third audible source/pure-tone clue and frequency comparison, rather than an inventory containing only strings and pipes. Keep distinct from the pipes. A small acoustic guitar or upright piano can be quietly visible too, for timbre and performance context.
D. A real SMALL FRIENDLY DOG sitting near the table, ears perked in relaxed attention toward the people/sound source. Nearby an OPEN NATURAL-HISTORY BOOK on the table with a LARGE CLEAR BAT PICTURE and an EAR illustration, no written text. These are natural hearing-range story clues; no bats flying indoors/daytime, no cartoon captions.
E. A modest HANDHELD SOUND-LEVEL METER lying on the table: small grey body, simple unlabelled LCD, microphone stalk with dark round foam at top, recognizable as one physical device, not a computer console. No numerical readings, no waveform on its display. This is a clue for comparing sound levels, not a hearing-protection/noise scene.
F. School everyday-talk AND concert/movie contexts in the same physical space: Xiaokui and Grandpa naturally talking/listening in front of a small CURTAINED PERFORMANCE STAGE or piano corner with a few chairs, and a discreet MOVIE-PROJECTOR / film-club display with clapperboard or film-reel motifs as a background item. It should feel like preparing a school sound exhibition linking conversation, music and cinema, not a studio recording session.
VERY IMPORTANT: No waveform screens, tablets, oscilloscopes, computer control desks, sinusoidal charts, physical sound ribbons, springs, water waves, scientific graphs, labels, prominent titles, speech bubbles, equation boards, logos or watermark. Sound is expressed through physical sources, human interaction and the listening dog. The open bat book is a small real object, not a floating data chart. No meteorites or chemistry glassware carried over from references. Don't imply a dog hears ultrasound from an ordinary musical note; it is simply listening. Keep all six groups coherent, distinguishable and readable at website-hero size.

COMPOSITION C01: A bright school multipurpose hall, balanced eye-level establishing shot. Xiaokui LEFT gently plucks the single-string sound box in the center-left foreground, Grandpa RIGHT listening and holding one tuning fork upright by the stem while smiling toward her. Spare unequal tuning fork and striker on its separate block. Three hollow pipe mouths clearly visible on a low support at front-right. Open bat/ear book and grey sound-level meter side-by-side near the front-center, separated from the strings. Small friendly dog seated beside the right table leg looking up attentively, fully visible. Behind them softly receding curtain stage, upright piano and a small movie-club projection corner with reel/clapperboard motif. Main focus remains the shared discovery between people, with each of the six prop/context groups visible. Similar warm approachable front-facing composition to the references, but fully new sound topic. The image should feel like the opening to a whole sound unit.
